passage:
Hey Anand,

You asked how the Pune job is going. It isn't. Three weeks ago the recruiter said on a call, "You are almost selected, just formalities." I told everyone at home. I stopped replying to two other companies, because why bother? Then nothing. I wrote once, politely, and again after a week. Still silence. I went from hopeful to confused to properly angry, and last night I wanted to send a nasty message. I didn't. This morning I reopened the mails from those two companies and apologised for the delay, and one has already given me a test date. I'm going to stop refreshing my inbox. If the recruiter ever writes back, fine.

Tarun

qa.q: How many times did Tarun write to the recruiter?
qa.a: Tarun wrote twice: once politely, and again after a week.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling by the end of the silence?
qa.a: Hopeful had turned to confused and then properly angry, to the point of wanting to send a nasty message.

qa.q: What did Tarun do that keeps other options open?
qa.a: Tarun reopened the mails from two other companies and apologised for the delay, and one has already given a test date.

qa.q: How might Anand read this email?
qa.a: Anand may feel for the frustration and be relieved that Tarun is choosing to move on instead of waiting.

grounding: A recruiter's 'almost selected' is followed by silence; Tarun follows up twice, keeps other applications alive and moves on.

passage: In Wardha, the only coaching centre for job exams had a noticeboard, and Alka had stopped reading it. Three weeks ago Karthik, a recruiter for a private insurance office in the district town, had called: 'You are almost selected. Just wait for the formal letter.' She had told her mother, turned down tuition work for the summer and stopped filling other forms. Then nothing. Two weeks of nothing. She went from checking her phone every hour to snapping at her little brother for borrowing it. Her old tuition teacher, Joshi-sir, heard it all at the bus stand. 'Don't stop your life for one maybe. Send two polite follow-ups, a week apart. Meanwhile fill those two forms on the board.' That evening Alka sent the first message to Karthik and filled one form at the cyber café. The second she would finish tomorrow.

qa.q: What did Karthik say when he called?
qa.a: Karthik said, 'You are almost selected. Just wait for the formal letter.'

qa.q: What was Alka feeling after two weeks of nothing?
qa.a: Alka felt confused and angry, her hope turning into irritation that she took out on her little brother.
Two polite follow-ups a week apart, while filling other forms, keeps one uncertain offer from holding her whole life still.

qa.q: How might Karthik see the 'almost selected' call?
qa.a: Karthik may have said it casually or before a final decision, not realising Alka would turn down work and stop applying because of it.

grounding: Shows the hope-then-silence of an 'almost selected' promise, and the advice to keep other applications alive and follow up politely twice.

passage: Bilal, the recruiter from a design agency in Hanoi, had shaken Tuan's hand after the final round and said, 'You're almost there, we just need sign-off.' That was five weeks ago. Tuan had declined a second interview at a smaller studio because it felt like cheating on the first. He hadn't renewed his room lease properly, thinking he might move closer to the agency. He had sent one polite email in week two and heard nothing. By week five he was angry at himself as much as at Bilal. His flatmate Linh asked, 'What happens if they never call?' Tuan didn't have an answer. That night he sent a second, final follow-up, short and friendly, and then wrote to the smaller studio: 'If the role is still open, I'd love to talk.' They replied by morning. He renewed the lease for another six months.

qa.q: How many weeks ago was the final round?
qa.a: The final round was five weeks ago.

qa.q: What was Tuan feeling by week five?
qa.a: Tuan felt angry and confused, at Bilal and at himself for putting life on hold.

qa.q: What would you advise someone in Tuan's position once the first follow-up goes unanswered?
qa.a: Send one more short, polite follow-up and keep other options open, as Tuan finally did with the smaller studio.

qa.q: What does Linh's question suggest Linh sees?
qa.a: Linh sees that Tuan has frozen life around one uncertain offer and gently points to it.

grounding: Shows a candidate who froze his plans after being told he was almost selected, then followed up a final time and revived other options.
